1	Design proposal for inter-plugin dependencies in HCLI and the IDA plugin manager. Produced through iterative discussion; the background research is in [[plugin manager dependency considerations]].
2	
3	## Problem
4	
5	Two use cases drive this work:
6	
7	1. Tightly-coupled plugin suites (high priority). Hex-Rays paid extensions are collections of plugins managed atomically. Users should not interact with individual members. This is a product packaging need.
8	
9	2. Curated plugin collections (lower priority). A community "Go Analysis Pack" installs several related plugins in one step. After installation the plugins retain their identity and can be managed independently. This is a discoverability/convenience need.
10	
11	## Design
12	
13	Two new optional fields on `PluginMetadata` in `ida-plugin.json`: `components` (tight coupling) and `dependencies` (loose coupling).
14	
15	### `components`
16	
17	Array of strings. Each entry is a subdirectory name that must contain its own `ida-plugin.json` with a matching `plugin.name`. Components are physically bundled inside the suite's archive, share the suite's lifecycle, and are hidden from users. Components can themselves declare `components`, nesting recursively (IDA recurses to depth 10).
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
22	  "plugin": {
23	    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
24	    "version": "2.1.0",
25	    "entryPoint": "init.py",
26	    "urls": { "repository": "https://plugins.hex-rays.com/hexrays/advanced-analysis/suite" },
27	    "authors": [{"name": "Hex-Rays", "email": "support@hex-rays.com"}],
28	    "idaVersions": ["9.3"],
29	
30	    "components": [
31	      "hexrays-taint-engine",
32	      "hexrays-type-propagation",
33	      "hexrays-call-graph-viz"
34	    ]
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	No version pins appear in the `components` array. The version of each component is whatever is physically present in the bundled archive, recorded in that component's own `ida-plugin.json`. This removes the need for a separate resolution and fetch step per component.
40	
41	### `dependencies`
42	
43	Array of strings. Each entry is `"name"` or `"name==version"` (pin optional). Declares plugins that are fetched individually and installed as independent top-level plugins, fully visible and independently manageable after installation.
44	
45	```json
46	{
47	  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
48	  "plugin": {
49	    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
50	    "version": "1.0.0",
51	    "entryPoint": "noop.py",
52	    "urls": { "repository": "https://github.com/community/go-analysis-pack" },
53	    "authors": [{"name": "Community", "email": "community@example.com"}],
54	
55	    "dependencies": [
56	      "go-runtime-detector",
57	      "go-string-extractor",
58	      "go-type-recovery"
59	    ]
60	  }
61	}
62	```
63	
64	### Validation rules
65	
66	Each `components` entry must match both a subdirectory name and the `plugin.name` in that subdirectory's `ida-plugin.json`. `dependencies` entries may use `==` for a version pin or omit a version (fetch latest).
67	
68	All `dependencies` entries must be resolvable from the declaring plugin's source. A plugin in the `hexrays` repo can only reference dependencies that also exist in that repo. The same applies to `community`, a local archive, or a local directory. No source prefix appears in the strings; source is inherited from the parent.
69	
70	All plugin names must be globally unique: across top-level plugins, components within the same suite, and components in other installed suites. HCLI validates this at install time by walking the full component tree recursively and checking against all installed manifests.
71	
72	## Filesystem layout
73	
74	```
75	$IDAUSR/plugins/
76	  hexrays-advanced-analysis/              <- suite (depth 1)
77	    ida-plugin.json                       <- suite manifest
78	    init.py                               <- suite entry point
79	    hexrays-taint-engine/                 <- component (depth 2)
80	      ida-plugin.json                     <- component manifest
81	      taint.py
82	    hexrays-type-propagation/             <- component (depth 2)
83	      ida-plugin.json
84	      typeprop.py
85	  go-analysis-pack/                       <- loose pack (depth 1)
86	    ida-plugin.json
87	    noop.py
88	  go-runtime-detector/                    <- standalone (depth 1)
89	    ida-plugin.json
90	    detector.py
91	  go-string-extractor/                    <- standalone (depth 1)
92	    ida-plugin.json
93	    strings.py
94	```
95	
96	IDA's `enumerate_fs_recursive()` (base/plugins.cpp:1557) recurses into every subdirectory up to depth 10, so it discovers all manifests in this layout. Each manifest must declare a unique `plugin.name`; duplicate names cause the second to be silently skipped. Entry points are resolved relative to their manifest's directory.
97	
98	## State management
99	
100	No extra state files. All relationship information is derived from installed manifests and the filesystem at runtime. To check whether a plugin belongs to a suite, walk the component trees declared by top-level manifests; `get_installed_plugin_records()` stays one-level-deep so nested components are naturally excluded from top-level listings. To enumerate a suite's components, read its `components` field and scan the corresponding subdirectories. To find a pack's declared dependencies, read its manifest.
101	
102	The filesystem is the source of truth for components (they live inside the suite directory). The manifest is the source of truth for dependencies (top-level plugins whose relationship to the pack exists only in the pack's `dependencies` field).
103	
104	If a suite is uninstalled but components somehow remain (interrupted operation, manual tampering), the orphaned components are standalone plugins at a non-standard depth. No broken state.
105	
106	## Behavior
107	
108	### Install
109	
110	**Suite with components (`hcli plugin install hexrays-advanced-analysis`):**
111	
112	1. Fetch the suite archive from source (repo, URL, or local path).
113	2. Scan all `ida-plugin.json` files in the archive. Walk `components` references recursively to build the full component tree.
114	3. Check for name collisions: every component name (at any depth) against existing top-level plugins and against each other.
115	4. Extract the archive to a staging directory. The existing `extract_zip_subdirectory_to()` extracts the suite's subtree, including all nested component subdirectories.
116	5. Validate that each `components` entry maps to a subdirectory whose `ida-plugin.json` has a matching `plugin.name`. Walk recursively.
117	6. Install Python dependencies declared by the suite and by every component in the tree.
118	7. Move staging to `$IDAUSR/plugins/<suite-name>/`.
119	
120	If a component name collides with a standalone install, warn and require `--force` to replace.
121	
122	**Pack with dependencies (`hcli plugin install go-analysis-pack`):**
123	
124	1. Fetch pack archive from source.
125	2. Parse `dependencies`. For each, fetch from the pack's source (latest compatible or pinned version).
126	3. Install pack to `$IDAUSR/plugins/<pack-name>/`.
127	4. Install each dependency to `$IDAUSR/plugins/<dep-name>/`. Skip if already installed at a satisfying version.
128	
129	**Standalone install of a component (`hcli plugin install -e ./hexrays-taint-engine`):**
130	
131	Works normally for development purposes. If the name collides with an existing suite component, error with: "hexrays-taint-engine is a component of hexrays-advanced-analysis; uninstall the suite first, or use --force to replace."
132	
133	### Upgrade
134	
135	**Suite upgrade:**
136	
137	1. Fetch the new suite archive from source.
138	2. Replace the entire suite directory atomically (trash-and-rename). Dropped components disappear with the old directory. New components appear in the replacement. Changed components update.
139	3. Install any new or changed Python dependencies across all members.
140	4. All-or-nothing: if extraction or Python dependency installation fails, roll back using the existing trash-based mechanism.
141	
142	**Loose pack upgrade:**
143	
144	1. Upgrade the pack plugin itself.
145	2. If the new manifest added dependencies, fetch and install them.
146	3. If the new manifest dropped dependencies, those plugins stay installed. The user can remove them manually.
147	4. Existing dependencies are not upgraded; they upgrade independently via `hcli plugin upgrade <dep>`.
148	
149	### Uninstall
150	
151	**Suite uninstall (`hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-advanced-analysis`):**
152	
153	```
154	hexrays-advanced-analysis manages these plugins:
155	  hexrays-taint-engine        2.1.0
156	  hexrays-type-propagation    2.0.0
157	  hexrays-call-graph-viz      1.5.0
158	Uninstall all? [Y/n]
159	```
160	
161	Default yes. Removes the suite directory and everything in it. In non-interactive mode, cascades without prompting.
162	
163	**Component uninstall (`hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-taint-engine`):**
164	
165	```
166	hexrays-taint-engine is a component of hexrays-advanced-analysis.
167	```
168	
169	Refused. Components are not individually uninstallable. The user must uninstall the suite.
170	
171	**Loose pack uninstall (`hcli plugin uninstall go-analysis-pack`):**
172	
173	```
174	Uninstalled go-analysis-pack.
175	These plugins were listed as dependencies:
176	  go-runtime-detector    2.0.0
177	  go-string-extractor    1.2.0
178	  go-type-recovery       0.9.1
179	Remove them too? [y/N]
180	```
181	
182	Default no. In non-interactive mode, does not cascade. The dependency list is read from the pack's manifest before deleting it.
183	
184	### Status display
185	
186	```
187	$ hcli plugin status
188	hexrays-advanced-analysis     2.1.0    (3 components)
189	go-analysis-pack              1.0.0
190	go-runtime-detector           2.0.0
191	go-string-extractor           1.2.0
192	go-type-recovery              0.9.1
193	my-standalone-plugin          3.0.0
194	```
195	
196	Components are not listed individually. The suite shows a component count derived by reading its `components` field and scanning subdirectories. A `--verbose` or `--show-components` flag expands them:
197	
198	```
199	$ hcli plugin status --show-components
200	hexrays-advanced-analysis     2.1.0
201	  hexrays-taint-engine        2.1.0    (component)
202	  hexrays-type-propagation    2.0.0    (component)
203	  hexrays-call-graph-viz      1.5.0    (component)
204	...
205	```
206	
207	JSON output includes a `components` array on suite entries, with each component's name and version read from its nested manifest.
208	
209	## Why two fields instead of one
210	
211	The background research recommends a single `dependencies` field with the "metapackage" pattern (apt, Home Assistant, Neovim distros). We started there but split into two fields because the two use cases have fundamentally different filesystem and lifecycle semantics:
212	
213	| | Components | Dependencies |
214	|---|---|---|
215	| Install location | Nested inside parent dir | Top-level, independent dir |
216	| Visible to user | No | Yes |
217	| Individually manageable | No | Yes |
218	| Lifecycle | Atomic with parent | Independent |
219	| Version | Implicit (bundled) | Optional pin |
220	| Upgrade | Replaced with parent | Independent |
221	| Uninstall | Removed with parent | Stay installed |
222	| Distribution | Physically inside archive | Fetched individually |
223	
224	This is *not* the VS Code split. VS Code's `extensionPack` and `extensionDependencies` both install members as top-level extensions with independent identity, differing only in uninstall cascading behavior. That creates conflicting ownership: an extension can be both a pack member and a functional dependency of something else, producing bugs (#169109, #64436, #55055).
225	
226	Our split avoids these bugs by making the two categories structurally disjoint.
227	
228	Components live inside the suite directory and are not addressable from outside. No external plugin can reference a component in its own `dependencies`. The conflict behind VS Code #169109 (can't uninstall pack because an external extension depends on a member) cannot arise: there is no mechanism for an external plugin to hold a reference to a component.
229	
230	Replacing or removing the suite directory removes all components. The orphan problem behind VS Code #64436 (dropped member stays installed forever) cannot occur because the filesystem is the membership record. When a new suite archive drops a component, the directory replacement removes it.
231	
232	Uninstalling a suite removes its directory, including all components. Uninstalling a loose pack removes only the pack. There is no "remove members except those that are dependencies of something else" logic (VS Code #55055). The uninstall path has no conditional cascading.
233	
234	## Distribution
235	
236	Components are distributed as part of their suite's archive. The archive physically contains the suite manifest and all nested component directories with their own manifests. Suite archives are constructed manually and added directly to the private `hexrays` repo as single entries. Offline bundles work the same way. From a local directory during development, the suite directory contains component subdirectories directly.
237	
238	Dependencies in a loose pack are fetched individually from the same source as the pack. Each dependency is its own repo entry, archive, or directory.
239	
240	## Implementation notes
241	
242	The current `install_plugin_archive()` library function already handles multi-manifest archives correctly: it searches for the manifest matching the requested name and extracts that plugin's subtree, including nested subdirectories. Five call sites in `src/hcli/commands/plugin/install.py` enforce a single-manifest constraint (`len(items) != 1`) that must be relaxed for suite archives. The repo-based install path already skips this check.
243	
244	`get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive()` in `src/hcli/lib/ida/plugin/__init__.py` already enumerates every `ida-plugin.json` in an archive. This provides the pre-extraction scan needed for name collision detection and component tree validation.
245	
246	New work: recursive component tree walking (for validation, Python dep collection, name collision checking, and status display), relaxing the single-manifest CLI checks, and recursive Python dependency installation across all suite members.
247	
248	## Scope (v1)
249	
250	v1 includes the `components` field (physically bundled, nested directory layout) and `dependencies` field (fetched individually, top-level install), with all the install/upgrade/uninstall behavior described above. Name collision validation (recursive), status display with component counts, recursive Python dependency installation for suite members, lint validation for the new fields, and JSON schema updates are also in scope.
251	
252	Deferred: `afterDependencies` for soft/load-order deps (no use case yet), `recommends` for optional-but-default installs (unclear UX), inter-plugin version ranges (every surveyed plugin manager advises against them), an `autoremove` command (suggest-on-uninstall is sufficient at IDA's plugin scale), and activation guards (IDA loads what it finds regardless).
253	
254	## Resolved questions
255	
256	1. **Suite entry point purpose.** The suite's entry point is a real plugin. It can register global menus, icons, settings UI, or other suite-level functionality. It is not a no-op marker.
257	
258	2. **Component visibility in IDA's UI.** Acceptable. Components appear in IDA's Edit > Plugins menu because IDA discovers their manifests. Plugin flags can hide them from that menu when desired.
259	
260	3. **Plugin name uniqueness.** All plugin names must be globally unique across top-level plugins, components within suites, and components across different suites. IDA silently skips duplicate `plugin.name` values, so HCLI validates uniqueness at install time.
261	
262	4. **Pack entry point.** A loose pack whose sole purpose is declaring `dependencies` still requires an `entryPoint` (schema constraint). Use a `noop.py`. Omitting `entryPoint` is not supported at this time.
263	
264	5. **Repo indexer and suites.** The indexer is not updated for suites in v1. Tight bundles are constructed manually and added to the private plugin repo, where the community indexer is not used.
265

## Test Structure for the Plugin System

### Directory layout
```
tests/
  conftest.py              -- autouse fixtures: probe cache clear, CliRunner stream pinning
  lib/
    fixtures.py            -- shared fixtures: temp dirs, env vars, virtual IDA environments
    test_plugin_install.py       -- core install/uninstall/upgrade lib + CLI tests
    test_plugin_records.py       -- installed plugin record queries, case-insensitive lookup
    test_plugin_collisions.py    -- repo-level name collisions, host disambiguation, status
    test_plugin_dependencies.py  -- loose dependency tests (recently added)
    test_plugin_dependency_migration.py  -- create-environment dep migration flow
    test_plugin_bundle.py        -- offline bundle manifest, repo, wheelhouse
    test_plugin_bundle_commands.py -- CLI for bundle info/create
    test_plugin.py               -- (likely metadata parsing)
    test_plugin_index.py         -- (repo indexing)
    test_plugin_pep723.py        -- PEP 723 inline script deps
    test_plugin_reference.py     -- plugin reference parsing
    test_plugin_settings.py      -- per-plugin config
  data/plugins/
    plugin1/                     -- fixture source dirs (src-v1..src-v6) + pre-built .zip files
    zydisinfo/                   -- binary plugin fixture
  integration/                   -- integration tests (download, full CLI flows)
```

### Key fixtures (from `fixtures.py`)
- **`virtual_ida_environment`** — sets `HCLI_IDAUSR` to a temp dir, fakes `HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_PLATFORM` and `HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_VERSION`. Allows plugin operations without a real IDA install.
- **`virtual_ida_environment_with_venv`** — extends above with a real Python venv at `$IDAUSR/venv`, setting `HCLI_CURRENT_IDA_PYTHON_EXE` and `VIRTUAL_ENV`. Needed for pip-related tests.
- **`block_network`** — sets HTTP(S)_PROXY to a dead endpoint for airgapped tests.
- **`temp_env_var` / `temp_env_var_path`** — context managers for env var manipulation (also syncs `hcli.env.ENV` attributes).
- **`set_env_var` / `unset_env_var`** — monkeypatch-based versions for pytest fixtures.

### How plugin archives are created in tests

**Two approaches:**

1. **Pre-built zip fixtures** on disk under `tests/data/plugins/`. E.g. `plugin1-v1.0.0.zip` with internal structure `src-v1/ida-plugin.json` + `src-v1/plugin1.py`. Used by `test_plugin_install.py` and integration tests.

2. **Programmatic in-memory zip creation** via helper functions, used in dependency and collision tests:
   - `_make_plugin_zip(name, version, deps=None)` in `test_plugin_dependencies.py` — creates a minimal zip `{name}/ida-plugin.json` + `{name}/{name}.py` with optional `dependencies` field.
   - `_make_plugin_metadata(name, version, deps=None)` — constructs the metadata dict.
   - `_make_fs_repo(archives)` — creates a temporary `FileSystemPluginRepo` from dict of `{filename: zip_bytes}`.
   - `make_plugin_zip(source_zip, dest_path, new_name=None, ...)` in `test_plugin_collisions.py` — derives a new zip from an existing fixture by rewriting `ida-plugin.json` fields. Used for collision/host disambiguation tests.
   - `_place_plugin(name, metadata)` in `test_plugin_dependency_migration.py` — writes plugin directory directly into `$IDAUSR/plugins/` without going through install flow.

### Existing dependency tests (`test_plugin_dependencies.py`)
Covers the **loose dependency** (`dependencies` field) use case:
- `parse_dependency_spec` — bare name, pinned version, with host, rejects invalid formats
- `PluginMetadata.dependencies` field — serialization, validation, empty/present
- `install_dependencies` integration — install deps from FS repo, skip already-installed, upgrade outdated pinned, no-downgrade, partial failure, local-dir warning
- Upgrade with dependencies — new deps installed, dropped deps reported, unsatisfied deps upgraded
- Uninstall CLI — lists deps, `--yes` removes deps, non-interactive keeps deps
- Lint validation — valid/invalid dependency specs

### No existing component/suite test infrastructure
There are **no tests for the `components` field**, no suite archive fixtures, and no helpers for creating nested component directories within archives. The `_make_plugin_zip` helper produces flat single-plugin archives. A suite test will need:
- A helper that creates multi-manifest archives (suite + nested component dirs)
- Test fixtures with component subdirectories inside parent plugin dir
- Collision detection tests for component names vs. top-level plugins
- Status display tests showing component counts and `--show-components` expansion

### Status JSON output format
Current JSON output from `plugin status --json` returns entries like:
```json
{"name": "...", "version": "...", "installed": true, "kind": "installed", "upgrade_checked": true, "in_repository": true, "upgradable_to": "..."}
```
The `kind` field exists but only reports `"installed"`. Components will need a new kind or additional fields.</result>

**Task: Research upgrade, uninstall, status, lint commands and existing dependency behavior**

## 1. Upgrade (`src/hcli/commands/plugin/upgrade.py`)

**Flow:**
- Lines 55–191: `upgrade_plugin(ctx, plugin, no_build_isolation)`
- Sweeps trash, resolves IDA env, validates plugin spec (rejects local files/URLs)
- Finds installed plugin via `find_installed_plugin(ref.name)` (line 87) — anchors upgrade to installed host
- Saves `old_deps = list(installed.metadata.plugin.dependencies)` (line 93) before upgrade
- Fetches new archive from plugin repo
- Calls `upgrade_plugin_archive(buf, plugin_name, ...)` (from `install.py` lib, line 1111)

**Upgrade implementation** (`src/hcli/lib/ida/plugin/install.py:1111–1174`):
- Validates metadata, checks platform/IDA version compat
- Rejects version downgrades
- `move_plugin_directory_to_trash(plugin_path, label=".rollback")` — atomic rename into trash
- Calls `install_plugin_archive()` to install new version
- On failure: rolls back by renaming trash copy back
- On success: deletes rollback copy

**Dependency handling** (lines 193–242):
- `_handle_upgrade_dependencies()` compares old vs new deps
- Reports dropped deps ("these dependencies were removed... they remain installed")
- Calls `install_dependencies()` for new deps

## 2. Uninstall (`src/hcli/commands/plugin/uninstall.py`)

**Flow** (lines 25–89):
- Before uninstalling, reads `record.metadata.plugin.dependencies` to capture dep names (lines 31–39)
- Calls `uninstall_plugin_impl(plugin)` — the library function
- Library function (`install.py:1022–1058`): handles symlinks (editable installs) vs directories, uses `remove_plugin_directory()` (trash-and-delete)
- After uninstall, lists installed deps and asks "Remove them too?" (default **no**, line 74)
- Non-interactive mode: prints "Remove them manually" and returns (line 77)
- With `--yes`: cascades removal

## Current State

The `dependencies` (loose coupling) field is fully implemented: install fetches deps independently, upgrade handles added/dropped deps, uninstall offers to cascade-remove deps, lint validates specs. No `components` field exists anywhere yet.

Several existing behaviors already work in our favor:

- `pack_plugin_directory_to_zip()` recurses — local directory installs of suites will include components
- `upgrade_plugin_archive()` does trash-and-replace of the whole directory — suite upgrades are atomically correct
- `uninstall_plugin()` removes the whole directory — suite removal takes components with it
- `get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive()` already enumerates every `ida-plugin.json` in an archive
- Archive lint already iterates all manifests

The main work is: adding the field, building component tree walking logic, relaxing multi-manifest constraints, adding collision checking, and wiring awareness into each command.

---

## Proposed Steps

### Step 1: Add `components` field to `PluginMetadata`

Add `components: list[str] = []` to the Pydantic model in `__init__.py`. Similar to `dependencies` but no version pins, no `@host` syntax — just bare directory/plugin names. Add a field validator that rejects entries with `==` or `@`. The JSON schema auto-updates from Pydantic.

### Step 2: Component tree walking utilities

The core building block everything else uses. Two variants needed:

- **From a directory** (for installed plugins): Given a plugin directory, read its `components` field, iterate subdirectories, read their manifests, recurse. Returns a flat list of `(relative_path, metadata)` tuples. Depth-limited to 10 (matching IDA's `enumerate_fs_recursive`).

- **From an archive** (for pre-install validation): Given zip bytes and a root manifest, walk the `components` references, find matching manifests in the archive, recurse. Returns the same flat list shape.

Both validate along the way: each `components` entry must map to a subdirectory whose `ida-plugin.json` has a matching `plugin.name`. These go in `src/hcli/lib/ida/plugin/` as a new module or in the existing `__init__.py`.

### Step 3: Name collision checking

New function: given a set of component names being installed, check against:
1. All top-level installed plugins (`get_installed_plugin_records()`)
2. All components of all installed suites (walk each installed suite's component tree)
3. Each other within the new suite (detect duplicates in the tree itself)

Returns collisions with context: "hexrays-taint-engine collides with a component of hexrays-advanced-analysis" or "collides with standalone plugin hexrays-taint-engine". The `--force` flag overrides collisions with standalone plugins (replaces them).

### Step 4: Root manifest identification for multi-manifest archives

For non-repo installs (local dir, local zip, URLs), the current code rejects archives with multiple manifests. For suites, we need to identify the root: the manifest whose name is NOT referenced in any other manifest's `components` field. If exactly one such manifest exists, it's the root. If zero or more than one, error.

### Step 5: Relax single-manifest CLI constraints

Change the 5 `len(items) != 1` checks in `install.py` (lines 133, 141, 150, 168, 182). Instead of rejecting multi-manifest archives, use the root identification logic from Step 4. If the archive is a valid suite structure, proceed with the root manifest name. If it's truly ambiguous (multiple unrelated plugins in one zip), still reject.

### Step 6: Recursive Python dependency collection

In `_install_plugin_archive()`, after extracting, walk the installed suite's component tree and collect `python_dependencies` from all component manifests in addition to the suite manifest. Pass the combined list to `pip_install_packages()`. This is the only change to the existing install library function beyond what extraction already handles.

### Step 7: Uninstall component awareness

Two new behaviors in `uninstall.py`:

1. **Component uninstall refused.** Before uninstalling, check if the target name is a component of any installed suite (walk all suite component trees). If so: `"hexrays-taint-engine is a component of hexrays-advanced-analysis."` — refuse.

2. **Suite uninstall confirmation.** If the target has a non-empty `components` field, list all components with versions and ask "Uninstall all? [Y/n]" (default yes). Non-interactive mode cascades without prompting. The actual removal is unchanged — deleting the suite directory removes everything.

### Step 8: Upgrade component awareness

The trash-and-replace mechanism already handles suite upgrades atomically. The only addition: collect Python dependencies from all component manifests in the new version (same logic as Step 6). The existing dependency-change reporting (`_handle_upgrade_dependencies`) continues to work for the suite's `dependencies` field.

### Step 9: Status display

Three changes in `status.py`:

1. **Component count.** When building `InstalledPluginStatusEntry`, if the plugin has `components`, walk its component tree and count. Display as `(3 components)` in text output.

2. **`--show-components` flag.** When set, expand suite entries to show each component indented below with name, version, and `(component)` tag.

3. **JSON output.** Add a `components` array to suite entries containing each component's name and version.

### Step 10: Lint validation

Add to `_lint_plugin_directory()` and `_lint_plugin_archive()`:

1. Each `components` entry must correspond to a subdirectory (or archive path) containing an `ida-plugin.json`.
2. The `plugin.name` in that manifest must match the `components` entry string.
3. No duplicate names across the component tree.
4. Recurse into components that themselves declare `components`.
5. Validate each component's manifest with the existing `_lint_metadata()`.

### Step 11: Standalone component install collision

When installing a plugin (any path), after resolving the name, check if that name is already a component of an installed suite. If so: `"hexrays-taint-engine is a component of hexrays-advanced-analysis; uninstall the suite first, or use --force to replace."` This uses the same collision checking from Step 3.

### Step 12: Tests

- **Helper**: `_make_suite_zip(suite_name, version, components=[...])` that creates a multi-manifest archive with nested component subdirectories.
- **Install tests**: suite installs, name collision detection, `--force` override, recursive python deps
- **Uninstall tests**: suite cascading confirmation, component refusal
- **Upgrade tests**: atomic replacement, component changes (added/dropped/changed)
- **Status tests**: component count, `--show-components`, JSON output
- **Lint tests**: valid/invalid component references, name uniqueness
- **Edge cases**: nested components (components declaring their own components), editable install of suite dir

---

## Concerns and decisions worth flagging

**Root detection for local installs.** The shallowest-manifest approach vs. the "not referenced by anyone" approach. I'm proposing the latter (find the manifest not referenced as a component by any other manifest) because depth alone is ambiguous if someone puts two unrelated plugins in one zip. The "not referenced" approach is semantically correct.

**Editable installs of suites.** `hcli plugin install -e ./suite-dir` creates a symlink. IDA recurses into symlink targets, so component subdirectories are discovered. No special handling needed. The only question is whether the symlink name must match the suite's `plugin.name` — it already must for regular editable installs, so this is consistent.

**Component-declares-components (nesting).** The design doc says "components can themselves declare components, nesting recursively (IDA recurses to depth 10)." All tree-walking logic needs the depth limit, and all validation/collection needs to be truly recursive, not just one level.

**No cross-suite component references.** The design explicitly forbids external plugins from referencing a component. This means no `dependencies` entry can name something that's a `components` entry of an installed suite. Should the install flow validate this? I'd say yes — if a plugin's `dependencies` lists a name that is a component of an installed suite, warn or error.

Implementation plan for the `components` field described in [[plugin components and dependencies design]]. The `dependencies` field is already implemented. This plan covers only the remaining `components` work.

## Step 1: Add `components` field to `PluginMetadata`

Add `components: list[str] = []` to the Pydantic model in `src/hcli/lib/ida/plugin/__init__.py`, alongside the existing `dependencies` field. Add a `@field_validator` that rejects entries containing `==` or `@` (components are bare directory names, no version pins or host qualifiers). The JSON schema auto-updates from Pydantic.

## Step 2: Component tree walking utilities

New module `src/hcli/lib/ida/plugin/components.py` with two functions that everything else builds on.

**From a directory** (for installed plugins): given a plugin directory path, read its manifest's `components` field, iterate the named subdirectories, read their manifests, validate that `plugin.name` matches the directory name, and recurse into each component's own `components`. Returns a flat list of `(relative_path, IDAMetadataDescriptor)` tuples. Depth-limited to 10 (matching IDA's `enumerate_fs_recursive`).

**From an archive** (for pre-install validation): given zip bytes and a root `IDAMetadataDescriptor`, walk the `components` references in the archive, find matching manifest paths, parse and validate, recurse. Returns the same shape. Raises on missing subdirectories, name mismatches, or depth exceeded.

Both functions validate as they walk: each `components` entry must map to a subdirectory whose `ida-plugin.json` has a `plugin.name` matching the entry string.

## Step 3: Name collision checking

New function in `components.py`: given a set of names from a component tree being installed, check against:

1. All top-level installed plugins (via `get_installed_plugin_records()`).
2. All components of all other installed suites (walk each installed suite's component tree using the directory walker from step 2).
3. Each other within the new suite (duplicates in the tree itself).

Returns a list of collisions with context messages like "hexrays-taint-engine collides with a component of hexrays-advanced-analysis" or "collides with standalone plugin hexrays-taint-engine".

Additionally, check that no `dependencies` entry (on the suite or any component) names something that is a component of an installed suite. Components are not addressable from outside their suite.

`--force` overrides collisions with standalone plugins (replaces them) but not collisions with other suites' components.

## Step 4: Root manifest identification

654	def parse_pep723_metadata(python_file_content: str) -> list[str]:
655	    """Parse PEP 723 inline script metadata from Python file content.
656	
657	    Returns a list of dependencies found in the PEP 723 metadata block,
658	    or an empty list if no metadata block is found.
659	
660	    Raises:
661	        ValueError: If metadata block is found but contains invalid TOML or unexpected data format
662	    """
663	    pattern = r"#\s*///\s*script\s*\n(.*?)#\s*///\s*\n"
664	    match = re.search(pattern, python_file_content, re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE)
665	
666	    if not match:
667	        return []
668	
669	    metadata_block = match.group(1)
670	
671	    lines = []
672	    for line in metadata_block.split("\n"):
673	        line = line.strip()
674	        if line.startswith("#"):
675	            line = line[1:].strip()
676	        if line:
677	            lines.append(line)
678	
679	    toml_content = "\n".join(lines)
680	
681	    try:
682	        metadata = tomllib.loads(toml_content)
683	        dependencies = metadata.get("dependencies", [])
684	        if isinstance(dependencies, list):
685	            return dependencies
686	        else:
687	            raise ValueError(f"PEP 723 dependencies must be a list, got {type(dependencies).__name__}")  # noqa: TRY004
688	    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as e:
689	        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse PEP 723 TOML metadata: {e}") from e

186	        entries = list(trash_dir.iterdir())
187	    except Exception as e:
188	        logger.debug("could not enumerate trash directory: %s", e)
189	        return
190	
191	    for entry in entries:
192	        logger.debug("sweeping trash: %s", entry)
193	        try:
194	            if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
195	                shutil.rmtree(entry)
196	            else:
197	                entry.unlink()
198	        except OSError as e:
199	            logger.debug("could not sweep %s: %s", entry, e)
200

22	@click.command()

24	@click.option("--yes", "-y", is_flag=True, default=False, help="Confirm all prompts automatically.")
25	def uninstall_plugin(plugin: str, yes: bool) -> None:
26	    """Remove an installed plugin."""
27	    dep_names: list[str] = []
28	    try:
29	        sweep_trash()
30

32	            record = find_installed_plugin(plugin)

68	        console.print(f"  {name}{version_str}")
69	
70	    interactive = sys.stdin.isatty()
71	    if yes:

75	    else:
76	        console.print("Remove them manually if no longer needed.")
77	        return

79	    if not should_remove:

82	    for name, _ in installed_deps:

16	    explain_missing_current_installation_directory,
17	    find_current_ida_platform,
18	    find_current_ida_version,

20	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin import IDAMetadataDescriptor, get_metadata_from_plugin_archive
21	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.bundle import bundle_dependency_source
22	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.exceptions import PluginNotInstalledError
23	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.install import find_installed_plugin, sweep_trash, upgrade_plugin_archive
24	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.reference import normalize_plugin_host, parse_plugin_reference
25	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.repo import BasePluginRepo

31	
32	def _resolve_effective_repo(plugin_repo: BasePluginRepo, plugin_name: str, host: str) -> BasePluginRepo:
33	    """When the repo is an aggregate, return the child that owns the plugin."""
34	    from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.repo.aggregate import AggregatePluginRepo
35	
36	    if not isinstance(plugin_repo, AggregatePluginRepo):
37	        return plugin_repo
38	
39	    plugin = plugin_repo.get_plugin_by_name(plugin_name, host=host)
40	    owner_name = plugin_repo.repo_of(plugin)
41	    if owner_name is not None:
42	        return plugin_repo.get_child_repo(owner_name)
43	    return plugin_repo

45	
46	@click.command()
47	@click.pass_context
48	@click.argument("plugin")
49	@click.option(
50	    "--no-build-isolation",
51	    is_flag=True,
52	    default=False,
53	    help="Disable pip build isolation when installing Python dependencies",
54	)
55	def upgrade_plugin(ctx, plugin: str, no_build_isolation: bool) -> None:
56	    """Upgrade an installed plugin to the latest compatible version."""
57	    pip_options: PipOptions = ctx.obj.get("pip_options", PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT)
58	    if no_build_isolation:
59	        pip_options = dataclasses.replace(pip_options, no_build_isolation=True)
60	    check_environment = not ctx.obj.get("no_python_environment_check", False)
61	    plugin_spec = plugin
62	    try:
63	        sweep_trash()
64	
65	        current_ida_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
66	        current_ida_version = find_current_ida_version()
67	
68	        if Path(plugin_spec).exists() and plugin_spec.endswith(".zip"):
69	            raise ValueError("cannot upgrade using local file; uninstall/reinstall instead")
70	
71	        if plugin_spec.startswith("file://"):
72	            raise ValueError("cannot upgrade using local file; uninstall/reinstall instead")
73	
74	        if plugin_spec.startswith("https://"):
75	            raise ValueError("cannot upgrade using URL; uninstall/reinstall instead")
76	
77	        try:
78	            ref = parse_plugin_reference(plugin_spec)
79	        except ValueError as e:
80	            raise click.BadParameter(f"invalid plugin reference: {plugin_spec!r}: {e}")
81	
82	        # Resolve the installed plugin first so we can anchor the upgrade to
83	        # the repository the user currently has installed. This avoids
84	        # switching repositories implicitly and also resolves the host for
85	        # bare-name upgrades even when the repository has a colliding name.
86	        try:
87	            installed = find_installed_plugin(ref.name)
88	        except PluginNotInstalledError:
89	            console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: plugin '{ref.name}' is not installed")
90	            raise click.Abort()
91	
92	        old_deps = list(installed.metadata.plugin.dependencies)
93	
94	        if ref.host is not None and normalize_plugin_host(installed.host) != normalize_plugin_host(ref.host):
95	            console.print(
96	                f"[red]Error[/red]: installed plugin '{installed.name}' comes from {installed.host}, not {ref.host}"
97	            )
98	            console.print(
99	                "Upgrade cannot switch repositories. Uninstall first, then install the other qualified plugin."
100	            )
101	            raise click.Abort()
102	
103	        # Anchor the lookup to the installed host regardless of whether the
104	        # user supplied it. This is what makes bare-name upgrades work even
105	        # when the repository has a colliding name.
106	        bare_spec = ref.name + ref.version_spec
107	        logger.info("finding plugin in repository")
108	        # An upgrade is anchored to the installed name@host, so it may resolve
109	        # across every configured repository -- the plugin's identity, not the
110	        # default scope, decides which one answers. An explicit prefix narrows
111	        # that to one repository, mirroring the @host check above.
112	        if ref.repo:
113	            from hcli.commands.plugin import repo_for_reference
114	
115	            plugin_repo: BasePluginRepo = repo_for_reference(ctx, ref)
116	        else:
117	            plugin_repo = ctx.obj["plugin_repo"]
118	        try:
119	            plugin_name, buf = plugin_repo.fetch_compatible_plugin_from_spec(
120	                bare_spec, current_ida_platform, current_ida_version, host=installed.host
121	            )
122	        except (httpx.ConnectError, httpx.TimeoutException):
123	            console.print("[red]Cannot connect to plugin repository - network unavailable.[/red]")
124	            console.print("Please check your internet connection.")
125	            raise click.Abort()
126	
127	        effective_repo = _resolve_effective_repo(plugin_repo, plugin_name, installed.host)
128	        if isinstance(effective_repo, PluginBundleRepo) and not pip_options.has_custom_sources:
129	            from hcli.lib.ida.python import detect_current_python_version, merge_bundle_pip_options
130	
131	            current_python_version = detect_current_python_version()
132	            with bundle_dependency_source(effective_repo, current_ida_platform, current_python_version) as bundle_opts:
133	                if bundle_opts is None:
134	                    available = ", ".join(effective_repo.target_ids) or "none"
135	                    console.print(
136	                        f"[red]Error[/red]: plugin bundle does not include dependencies"
137	                        f" for {current_ida_platform}, Python {current_python_version}."
138	                    )
139	                    console.print(f"Available targets in this bundle: {available}")
140	                    raise click.Abort()
141	                effective_pip_options = merge_bundle_pip_options(pip_options, bundle_opts)
142	                upgrade_plugin_archive(
143	                    buf, plugin_name, pip_options=effective_pip_options, check_environment=check_environment
144	                )
145	        else:
146	            upgrade_plugin_archive(buf, plugin_name, pip_options=pip_options, check_environment=check_environment)
147	
148	        _, metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_archive(buf, plugin_name)
149	
150	        console.print(f"[green]Installed[/green] plugin: [blue]{plugin_name}[/blue]=={metadata.plugin.version}")
151	
152	        try:
153	            _handle_upgrade_dependencies(
154	                old_deps=old_deps,
155	                new_metadata=metadata,
156	                plugin_repo=plugin_repo,
157	                current_ida_platform=current_ida_platform,
158	                current_ida_version=current_ida_version,
159	                pip_options=pip_options,
160	                check_environment=check_environment,
161	            )
162	        except Exception as dep_err:
163	            logger.debug("dependency handling failed: %s", dep_err, exc_info=True)
164	            console.print(f"[yellow]Warning[/yellow]: failed to process dependencies: {dep_err}")
165	    except MissingCurrentInstallationDirectory:
166	        explain_missing_current_installation_directory(console)
167	        raise click.Abort()
168	
169	    except FailedToDetectIDAVersion:
170	        explain_failed_to_detect_ida_version(console)
171	        raise click.Abort()
172	
173	    except KeyError as e:
174	        # get_plugins() drops repositories it could not consult, so a miss here
175	        # may mean "your session expired", not "no such plugin". Say which.
176	        logger.debug("error: %s", e, exc_info=True)
177	        console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: {e}")
178	        aggregate = ctx.obj.get("plugin_repos")
179	        if aggregate is not None:
180	            for note in aggregate.notes():
181	                console.print(f"[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] repository {note}")
182	        raise click.Abort()
183	
184	    except click.Abort:
185	        raise
186	
187	    except Exception as e:
188	        logger.debug("error: %s", e, exc_info=True)
189	        console.print(f"[red]Error[/red]: {e}")
190	        raise click.Abort()
191	
192	
193	def _handle_upgrade_dependencies(
194	    *,
195	    old_deps: list[str],
196	    new_metadata: IDAMetadataDescriptor,
197	    plugin_repo: BasePluginRepo,
198	    current_ida_platform: str,
199	    current_ida_version: str,
200	    pip_options: PipOptions,
201	    check_environment: bool,
202	) -> None:
203	    from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.dependencies import install_dependencies
204	    from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.reference import parse_dependency_spec
205	
206	    new_deps = list(new_metadata.plugin.dependencies)
207	    if not old_deps and not new_deps:
208	        return
209	
210	    old_names = {parse_dependency_spec(s).name for s in old_deps}
211	    new_names = {parse_dependency_spec(s).name for s in new_deps}
212	
213	    dropped = old_names - new_names
214	    if dropped:
215	        console.print(
216	            f"[yellow]Note[/yellow]: these dependencies were removed from [blue]{new_metadata.plugin.name}[/blue]:"
217	        )
218	        for name in sorted(dropped):
219	            console.print(f"  {name}")
220	        console.print("They remain installed; remove them manually if no longer needed.")
221	
222	    if new_deps:
223	        console.print(f"Checking dependencies for [blue]{new_metadata.plugin.name}[/blue]...")
224	        with rich.status.Status("checking dependencies", console=stderr_console):
225	            result = install_dependencies(
226	                metadata=new_metadata,
227	                plugin_repo=plugin_repo,
228	                current_platform=current_ida_platform,
229	                current_version=current_ida_version,
230	                pip_options=pip_options,
231	                check_environment=check_environment,
232	            )
233	
234	        for name in result.installed:
235	            console.print(f"  [green]Installed[/green] dependency: [blue]{name}[/blue]")
236	        for name in result.upgraded:
237	            console.print(f"  [green]Upgraded[/green] dependency: [blue]{name}[/blue]")
238	        for name in result.skipped:
239	            console.print(f"  [dim]Skipped[/dim] dependency: {name} (already installed)")
240	        for name, error in result.failed:
241	            console.print(f"  [red]Failed[/red] dependency: {name}: {error}")
242

37	class InstalledPluginStatusEntry(BaseModel):

77	def _collect_installed_entry(

81	    current_ida_version: str,
82	    skip_upgrade_check: bool,

96	        )

104	                latest_version if parse_plugin_version(latest_version) > parse_plugin_version(record.version) else None
105	            ),

108	        return InstalledPluginStatusEntry(

117	def _render_status_row(table: rich.table.Table, entry: PluginStatusEntry) -> None:
118	    if isinstance(entry, IncompatiblePluginStatusEntry):
119	        table.add_row(
120	            f"[grey69](incompatible)[/grey69] [blue]{entry.name}[/blue]",
121	            entry.version or "",
122	            f"[grey69]found at: $IDAPLUGINS/[/grey69]{entry.path}",
123	        )
124	        return
125	
126	    if isinstance(entry, LegacyPluginStatusEntry):
127	        table.add_row(
128	            f"[grey69](legacy)[/grey69] [blue]{entry.name}[/blue]",
129	            "",
130	            f"[grey69]found at: $IDAPLUGINS/[/grey69]{entry.path}",
131	        )
132	        return
133	
134	    if isinstance(entry, NotFoundPluginStatusEntry):
135	        return
136	
137	    if not entry.upgrade_checked:
138	        status = "[dim]skipped[/dim]"
139	    elif not entry.in_repository:
140	        status = "[yellow]not found in repository[/yellow]"
141	    elif entry.upgradable_to:
142	        status = f"upgradable to [yellow]{entry.upgradable_to}[/yellow]"
143	    else:
144	        status = ""
145	
146	    table.add_row(entry.name, entry.version, status)

149	def collect_status_report(
150	    plugin_repo: BasePluginRepo,
151	    plugins: tuple[str, ...],
152	    skip_upgrade_check: bool,
153	) -> StatusReport:
154	    current_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
155	    current_ida_version = find_current_ida_version()
156	
157	    all_records = get_installed_plugin_records()
158	
159	    not_found_names: list[str] = []
160	    if plugins:
161	        installed_records = []
162	        for name in plugins:
163	            record = find_installed_plugin_in(all_records, name)
164	            if record is None:
165	                not_found_names.append(name)
166	            else:
167	                installed_records.append(record)
168	    else:
169	        installed_records = all_records
170	
171	    entries: list[PluginStatusEntry] = [
172	        _collect_installed_entry(plugin_repo, record, current_platform, current_ida_version, skip_upgrade_check)
173	        for record in installed_records
174	    ]
175	
176	    entries.extend(NotFoundPluginStatusEntry(name=name) for name in not_found_names)
177	
178	    if not plugins:
179	        plugin_directory = get_plugins_directory()
180	        for path, metadata in get_installed_minimal_plugins():
181	            plugin_path = path.parent.relative_to(plugin_directory)
182	            entries.append(
183	                IncompatiblePluginStatusEntry(
184	                    name=metadata.plugin.name,
185	                    version=metadata.plugin.version or None,
186	                    path=f"{plugin_path}/",
187	                )
188	            )
189	
190	        for path in get_installed_legacy_plugins():
191	            entries.append(
192	                LegacyPluginStatusEntry(
193	                    name=path.name,
194	                    path=path.name,
195	                )
196	            )
197	
198	    return StatusReport(plugins=entries)

201	def render_status_report_text(report: StatusReport, plugins_filter: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
202	    table = rich.table.Table(show_header=False, box=None)

204	    table.add_column("version", style="default")
205	    table.add_column("status")
206	
207	    not_found_names: list[str] = []
208	    has_incompatible = False
209	    has_legacy = False
210	
211	    for entry in report.plugins:
212	        if isinstance(entry, NotFoundPluginStatusEntry):
213	            not_found_names.append(entry.name)
214	            continue
215	        if isinstance(entry, IncompatiblePluginStatusEntry):
216	            has_incompatible = True
217	        elif isinstance(entry, LegacyPluginStatusEntry):
218	            has_legacy = True
219	        _render_status_row(table, entry)

221	    if table.row_count:

223	    elif not plugins_filter:

225	
226	    for name in not_found_names:

228	
229	    if has_incompatible:

231	        console.print("[yellow]Incompatible plugins[/yellow] don't work with this version of hcli.")
232	        console.print(
233	            f"[dim]They might be broken or outdated. Try using `{ENV.HCLI_BINARY_NAME} plugin lint /path/to/plugin`.[/dim]"
234	        )
235	
236	    if has_legacy:

238	        console.print("[yellow]Legacy plugins[/yellow] are old, single-file plugins.")
239	        console.print("They aren't managed by hcli. Try finding an updated version in the plugin repository.")
240

242	def render_status_report_json(report: StatusReport) -> None:
243	    print_json(report.model_dump(mode="json"))
244	
245	
246	@click.command()
247	@click.argument("plugins", nargs=-1)

249	    "--skip-upgrade-check",
250	    is_flag=True,
251	    default=False,
252	    help="skip the per-plugin upgrade check against the plugin repository",
253	)
254	@click.option("--json", "json_output", is_flag=True, default=False, help="output machine-readable JSON")
255	@click.pass_context
256	def get_plugin_status(ctx, plugins: tuple[str, ...], skip_upgrade_check: bool, json_output: bool) -> None:
257	    """Show installed plugins and their upgrade status.
258	
259	    If one or more PLUGINS are given, show status for just those plugins,

261	    """

263	    try:

266	        if json_output:

268	        else:

271	    except MissingCurrentInstallationDirectory:
272	        explain_missing_current_installation_directory(console)
273	        raise click.Abort()
274	
275	    except FailedToDetectIDAVersion:
276	        explain_failed_to_detect_ida_version(console)

496	def resolve_python_for_dependencies(python_dependencies: list[str], *, check_environment: bool = True) -> Path:
497	    """Find IDA's Python and, unless disabled, refuse environments where installing into it is pointless.
498	
499	    The environment check prints warnings to stderr for non-recommended but
500	    workable setups and raises for setups where the packages would never reach
501	    IDA (no venv, wrong Python version, PEP 668, uv overlay, no pip).
502	
503	    Raises:
504	        PythonNotFoundError: when IDA's Python can't be determined.
505	        DependencyInstallationError: when the environment check finds errors.
506	        PipNotAvailableError: when pip is missing and the environment check was skipped.
507	    """
508	    resolved = resolve_current_python()
509	    if check_environment:
510	        try:
511	            validate_python_environment(resolved)
512	        except PythonEnvironmentError as e:
513	            raise DependencyInstallationError(python_dependencies, str(e)) from e
514	
515	    if not has_pip(resolved.exe):
516	        logger.debug("pip not available")
517	        raise PipNotAvailableError(resolved.exe)
518	
519	    return resolved.exe

522	def validate_can_install_python_dependencies(
523	    zip_data: bytes,
524	    metadata: IDAMetadataDescriptor,
525	    excluded_plugins: list[str] | None = None,
526	    python_exe: Path | None = None,
527	    pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT,
528	    check_environment: bool = True,
529	) -> Path | None:
530	    """Verify Python dependencies can be installed.
531	
532	    Returns:
533	        The Python executable path if dependencies were validated, None if no dependencies needed.
534	
535	    Raises:
536	        PipNotAvailableError: If pip is not available in IDA's Python
537	        DependencyInstallationError: If dependencies cannot be installed, including when
538	            IDA's Python environment fails the health check (see `validate_python_environment`).
539	    """
540	    python_dependencies = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_archive(zip_data, metadata)
541	    if python_dependencies:
542	        all_python_dependencies: list[str] = []
543	        for existing_plugin_path in get_installed_plugin_paths():
544	            existing_metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(existing_plugin_path)
545	            if excluded_plugins and existing_metadata.plugin.name in excluded_plugins:
546	                continue
547	
548	            existing_deps = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_directory(existing_plugin_path, existing_metadata)
549	            all_python_dependencies.extend(existing_deps)
550	
551	        all_python_dependencies.extend(python_dependencies)
552	
553	        if python_exe is None:
554	            python_exe = resolve_python_for_dependencies(python_dependencies, check_environment=check_environment)
555	        elif not has_pip(python_exe):
556	            logger.debug("pip not available")
557	            raise PipNotAvailableError(python_exe)
558	        logger.debug(f"python: {python_exe}")
559	
560	        try:
561	            verify_pip_can_install_packages(python_exe, all_python_dependencies, pip_options=pip_options)
562	        except CantInstallPackagesError as e:
563	            logger.debug("can't install dependencies: %s", e)
564	            raise DependencyInstallationError(python_dependencies, str(e)) from e
565	
566	        return python_exe
567	
568	    return None

571	def validate_can_install_plugin(
572	    zip_data: bytes,
573	    metadata: IDAMetadataDescriptor,
574	    current_platform: str,
575	    current_version: str,
576	    pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT,
577	    check_environment: bool = True,
578	) -> Path | None:
579	    """Verify plugin can be installed.
580	
581	    Returns:
582	        The Python executable path if pip dependencies were validated, None otherwise.
583	
584	    Raises:
585	        InvalidPluginNameError: If plugin name is invalid
586	        PluginAlreadyInstalledError: If plugin is already installed
587	        BrokenPluginInstallationError: If remnants of a broken installation are in the way
588	        PlatformIncompatibleError: If current platform is not supported
589	        IDAVersionIncompatibleError: If current IDA version is not supported
590	        PipNotAvailableError: If pip is not available (when dependencies are needed)
591	        DependencyInstallationError: If dependencies cannot be installed
592	    """
593	    name = metadata.plugin.name
594	    try:
595	        destination_path = get_plugin_directory(name)
596	    except ValueError as e:
597	        logger.error(f"Can't install plugin: {e!s}")
598	        raise InvalidPluginNameError(name, str(e)) from e

"""Tests for tightly-coupled plugin components (suites)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import logging
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from click.testing import CliRunner
from fixtures import *
from pydantic import ValidationError

from hcli.commands.plugin import plugin as plugin_group
from hcli.lib.ida.plugin import IDAMetadataDescriptor, get_metadatas_with_paths_from_plugin_archive
from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.components import (
    check_component_name_collisions,
    collect_all_component_names_from_archive,
    find_root_manifest_in_archive,
    find_suite_for_component,
    walk_component_tree_from_archive,
    walk_component_tree_from_directory,
)
from hcli.lib.ida.plugin.install import (
    get_installed_plugin_records,
    install_plugin_archive,
    is_plugin_installed,
    uninstall_plugin,
    upgrade_plugin_archive,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

HOST = "https://github.com/test/test-suite"


def _make_plugin_metadata(
    name: str,
    version: str,
    *,
    components: list[str] | None = None,
    deps: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    plugin: dict = {
        "name": name,
        "version": version,
        "entryPoint": f"{name}.py",
        "urls": {"repository": HOST},
        "authors": [{"name": "Test", "email": "test@example.com"}],
    }
    if components is not None:
        plugin["components"] = components
    if deps is not None:
        plugin["dependencies"] = deps
    return {"IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1, "plugin": plugin}


def _make_standalone_zip(name: str, version: str, **kwargs) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    metadata = _make_plugin_metadata(name, version, **kwargs)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr(f"{name}/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(metadata))
        zf.writestr(f"{name}/{name}.py", "# plugin")
    return buf.getvalue()


def _make_suite_zip(
    suite_name: str,
    suite_version: str,
    components: list[tuple[str, str]],
    *,
    suite_deps: list[str] | None = None,
) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    comp_names = [name for name, _ in components]
    suite_meta = _make_plugin_metadata(suite_name, suite_version, components=comp_names, deps=suite_deps)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(suite_meta))
        zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{suite_name}.py", "# suite entry point")

        for comp_name, comp_version in components:
            comp_meta = _make_plugin_metadata(comp_name, comp_version)
            zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{comp_name}/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(comp_meta))
            zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{comp_name}/{comp_name}.py", "# component")

    return buf.getvalue()


def _make_nested_suite_zip(
    suite_name: str,
    suite_version: str,
    components: list[tuple[str, str, list[tuple[str, str]]]],
) -> bytes:
    """Create a suite with nested components (components that have their own components)."""
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    top_comp_names = [name for name, _, _ in components]
    suite_meta = _make_plugin_metadata(suite_name, suite_version, components=top_comp_names)

    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(suite_meta))
        zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{suite_name}.py", "# suite")

        for comp_name, comp_version, sub_components in components:
            sub_names = [n for n, _ in sub_components]
            comp_meta = _make_plugin_metadata(comp_name, comp_version, components=sub_names if sub_names else None)
            zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{comp_name}/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(comp_meta))
            zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{comp_name}/{comp_name}.py", "# component")

            for sub_name, sub_version in sub_components:
                sub_meta = _make_plugin_metadata(sub_name, sub_version)
                zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{comp_name}/{sub_name}/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(sub_meta))
                zf.writestr(f"{suite_name}/{comp_name}/{sub_name}/{sub_name}.py", "# sub-component")

    return buf.getvalue()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PluginMetadata.components field
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_metadata_with_components():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=["comp-a", "comp-b"])
    descriptor = IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)
    assert descriptor.plugin.components == ["comp-a", "comp-b"]


def test_metadata_without_components():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0")
    descriptor = IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)
    assert descriptor.plugin.components == []


def test_metadata_empty_components():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=[])
    descriptor = IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)
    assert descriptor.plugin.components == []


def test_metadata_rejects_version_pin_in_components():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=["comp-a==1.0.0"])
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="version pins"):
        IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)


def test_metadata_rejects_host_qualifier_in_components():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=["comp-a@https://github.com/x/y"])
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="host qualifiers"):
        IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)


def test_metadata_rejects_duplicate_component_names():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=["comp-a", "comp-a"])
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="unique"):
        IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)


def test_metadata_rejects_invalid_component_name():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=["bad name!"])
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)


def test_metadata_serialization_includes_components():
    data = _make_plugin_metadata("my-suite", "1.0.0", components=["comp-a", "comp-b"])
    descriptor = IDAMetadataDescriptor.model_validate(data)
    serialized = descriptor.model_dump(mode="json", by_alias=True)
    assert serialized["plugin"]["components"] == ["comp-a", "comp-b"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# find_root_manifest_in_archive
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_find_root_manifest_single_plugin():
    zip_data = _make_standalone_zip("my-plugin", "1.0.0")
    path, meta = find_root_manifest_in_archive(zip_data)
    assert meta.plugin.name == "my-plugin"


def test_find_root_manifest_in_suite():
    zip_data = _make_suite_zip("my-suite", "1.0.0", [("comp-a", "1.0.0"), ("comp-b", "2.0.0")])
    path, meta = find_root_manifest_in_archive(zip_data)
    assert meta.plugin.name == "my-suite"


def test_find_root_manifest_rejects_ambiguous():
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    meta_a = _make_plugin_metadata("plugin-a", "1.0.0")
    meta_b = _make_plugin_metadata("plugin-b", "1.0.0")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as zf:
        zf.writestr("plugin-a/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(meta_a))
        zf.writestr("plugin-a/plugin-a.py", "# a")
        zf.writestr("plugin-b/ida-plugin.json", json.dumps(meta_b))
        zf.writestr("plugin-b/plugin-b.py", "# b")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="multiple unrelated"):
        find_root_manifest_in_archive(buf.getvalue())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# walk_component_tree_from_archive
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_walk_archive_flat_suite():
    zip_data = _make_suite_zip("my-suite", "1.0.0", [("comp-a", "1.0.0"), ("comp-b", "2.0.0")])
    path, meta = find_root_manifest_in_archive(zip_data)
    tree = walk_component_tree_from_archive(zip_data, path, meta)
    names = {m.plugin.name for _, m in tree}
    assert names == {"comp-a", "comp-b"}


def test_walk_archive_nested_suite():
    zip_data = _make_nested_suite_zip(
        "my-suite", "1.0.0",
        [("comp-a", "1.0.0", [("sub-x", "0.1.0")]), ("comp-b", "2.0.0", [])],
    )
    path, meta = find_root_manifest_in_archive(zip_data)
    tree = walk_component_tree_from_archive(zip_data, path, meta)
    names = {m.plugin.name for _, m in tree}
    assert names == {"comp-a", "comp-b", "sub-x"}


def test_collect_all_component_names():
    zip_data = _make_suite_zip("my-suite", "1.0.0", [("comp-a", "1.0.0"), ("comp-b", "2.0.0")])
    path, meta = find_root_manifest_in_archive(zip_data)
    names = collect_all_component_names_from_archive(zip_data, path, meta)
    assert names == {"comp-a", "comp-b"}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install suite
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_install_suite(virtual_ida_environment):
    zip_data = _make_suite_zip("my-suite", "1.0.0", [("comp-a", "1.0.0"), ("comp-b", "2.0.0")])

def test_uninstall_suite_removes_components(virtual_ida_environment):

24	### ida-plugin.json
25	
26	The [`ida-plugin.json` file](https://docs.hex-rays.com/developer/publishing-plugins/how-tos/plugin-publishing) is the marker for an IDA Pro plugin.
27	A typical `ida-plugin.json` file might look like this:

31	  "$schema": "https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json",
32	  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
33	  "plugin": {
34	    "name": "oplog",
35	    "entryPoint": "oplog_entry.py",
36	    "version": "0.1.2",
37	    "idaVersions": ["9.1", "9.2"],
38	    "description": "oplog is an IDA Pro plugin that records operations during analysis.",
39	    "license": "Apache 2.0",
40	    "categories": [
41	      "ui-ux-and-visualization"
42	    ],
43	    "pythonDependencies": ["pydantic>=2"],
44	    "urls": {
45	      "repository": "https://github.com/williballenthin/idawilli"
46	    },
47	    "authors": [{
48	      "name": "Willi Ballenthin",
49	      "email": "wballenthin@hex-rays.com"
50	    }],
51	    "keywords": [
52	      "activity-tracking",
53	      "workflow-analysis",
54	      "reverse-engineering-methodology",
55	      "ai-training-data",
56	      "analysis-visualization"
57	    ]
58	  }
59	}
60	```
61	
62	And a minimal `ida-plugin.json` could look like this:
63	
64	```json
65	{
66	  "$schema": "https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json",
67	  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
68	  "plugin": {
69	    "name": "oplog",
70	    "entryPoint": "oplog_entry.py",
71	    "version": "0.1.2",
72	    "urls": {
73	      "repository": "https://github.com/williballenthin/idawilli"
74	    },
75	    "authors": [{
76	      "name": "Willi Ballenthin",
77	      "email": "wballenthin@hex-rays.com"
78	    }]
79	  }
80	}
81	```
82	
83	In addition to the primary fields described initially on the [Hex-Rays docs](https://docs.hex-rays.com/developer/publishing-plugins/how-tos/plugin-publishing), **HCLI compatibility added new, required fields** in `ida-plugin.json`:
84	
85	  - `version`: the version of the plugin archive
86	  - `urls.repository`: the repository that publishes the plugin
87	  - `authors` (or `maintainers`): name and/or email. Social media handles are ok!
88	
89	And there are new optional fields:
90	
91	  - `.plugin.pythonDependencies` is a list of packages on PyPI that will be installed
92	  - `.plugin.keywords` is a list of terms to help users searching for plugins
93	  - `.plugin.platforms` is recommended, defaults to all platforms. The possible values are: `windows-x86_64`, `linux-x86_64`, `macos-x86_64`, and `macos-aarch64`.
94	  - `.plugin.license` for the code license of your project
95	  - `.plugin.settings` is a list of descriptors of settings
96	  - `.plugin.dependencies` declares companion plugins to install alongside this one (e.g., `["dep-a", "dep-b==1.0.0"]`)
97	
98	If there's a problem with the `ida-plugin.json` file, then the plugin is invalid and won't work with the repo.
99	Unfortunately even things like trailing commas will break strict JSON parsers like the one used by HCLI.
100	So, you can use `hcli plugin lint /path/to/plugin[.zip]` to check for problems and suggestions.
101	
102	!!! tip "Editor validation with JSON Schema"
103	
104	    HCLI publishes a JSON Schema for `ida-plugin.json` at
105	    [`https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json`](https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json).
106	
107	    Reference it from the top of your `ida-plugin.json` to get inline validation,
108	    autocompletion, and hover documentation in editors like VSCode:
109	
110	    ```json
111	    {
112	      "$schema": "https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json",
113	      "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
114	      "plugin": { ... }
115	    }
116	    ```
117	
118	    The schema is generated from the same Pydantic models HCLI uses to validate
119	    plugins, so editor warnings match what `hcli plugin lint` will report.
120	
121	
122	### Shared Settings
123	
124	HCLI is aware of settings that plugins declare in `ida-plugin.json` and prompts users for their value
125	during installation. The settings are written into `ida-config.json` and can be queried at plugin runtime
126	using the [ida-settings](https://pypi.org/project/ida-settings/) (v3) Python package:
127	
128	```py
129	import ida_settings
130	
131	api_key = ida_settings.get_current_plugin_setting("openai_key")
132	```
133	
134	Plugin authors are encouraged to adopt this configuration system, as it provides a centralized way to manage edits from both the CLI and (eventually) the GUI, users don't have to manually edit source code/config files,
135	and the data can be easily exported/imported.
136	
137	!!! note "Coming Soon"
138	
139	      The associated IDA plugin `ida-settings-editor` that lets users configure plugin settings within IDA is not yet available. We plan to introduce it in a future release.
140	
141	#### Setting Fields
142	
143	Each setting in the `settings` array supports the following fields:
144	
145	| Field | Type | Required | Description |
146	|-------|------|----------|-------------|
147	| `key` | string | yes | Unique code-level identifier (e.g., `"api_key"`) |
148	| `type` | string | yes | Either `"string"` or `"boolean"` |
149	| `required` | boolean | yes | Whether the setting must be provided |
150	| `default` | string/boolean | no | Default value when not configured |
151	| `name` | string | yes | Human-readable name (e.g., `"OpenAI API key"`) |
152	| `documentation` | string | no | Human-readable explanation |
153	| `validation_pattern` | string | no | Regex pattern for string validation |
154	| `choices` | array | no | List of acceptable string values |
155	| `prompt` | boolean | no | Whether to prompt during installation (default: `true`) |
156	
157	Setting `"prompt": false` is useful for advanced or niche settings that have sensible defaults and shouldn't clutter the installation experience. These settings can still be configured later via `hcli plugin config`.
158	
159	Example settings configuration:
160	
161	```json
162	{
163	  "settings": [
164	    {
165	      "key": "api_key",
166	      "type": "string",
167	      "required": true,
168	      "name": "API Key",
169	      "documentation": "Your API key from https://example.com/keys"
170	    },
171	    {
172	      "key": "cache_size",
173	      "type": "string",
174	      "required": false,
175	      "default": "100",
176	      "name": "Cache Size",
177	      "documentation": "Maximum number of cached items",
178	      "prompt": false
179	    }
180	  ]
181	}
182	```
183	
184	
185	### Plugin Dependencies
186	
187	A plugin can declare other plugins as loose dependencies via the `dependencies` field. Each entry is a plugin reference: a bare name, a name with a version pin, or a name with a repository host URL and optional version pin.
188	
189	```json
190	{
191	  "plugin": {
192	    "dependencies": [
193	      "go-runtime-detector",
194	      "go-string-extractor==1.2.0",
195	      "helper@https://github.com/org/repo"
196	    ]
197	  }
198	}
199	```
200	
201	When a user installs or upgrades a plugin that declares dependencies, HCLI fetches each one from the same repository and installs it as an independent top-level plugin. Dependencies that are already installed and satisfy the spec are skipped. If a pinned dependency is installed at a lower version, it is upgraded automatically; a higher installed version is not downgraded.
202	
203	Dependencies are not bundled inside the declaring plugin's archive. Each dependency is its own plugin with its own `ida-plugin.json` and its own archive in the repository.
204	
205	### Source Archives and Binary Archives
206	
207	For many pure-Python IDA plugins, source archives are often sufficient.
208	This means you don't have to create any GitHub Actions workflows; you just have to tag your releases in GitHub.
209	
210	If you distribute your pure-Python IDA plugin via PyPI, [like IPyIDA does](https://github.com/eset/ipyida),
211	then the plugin directory in your source archive becomes very simple.
212	You can put the following content in a subdirectory of the project (preferred), or publish a separate repository for the metadata:
213	
214	
215	```
216	.
217	├── ida-plugin.json
218	└── entry_stub.py
219	```
220	
221	With `ida-plugin.json`:
222	
223	```json
224	{
225	  "$schema": "https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json",
226	  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
227	  "plugin": {
228	    "name": "plugin1",
229	    "entryPoint": "entry_stub.py",
230	    "version": "1.0",
231	    "idaVersions": ["9.0", "9.1", "9.2"],
232	    "pythonDependencies": ["ida-plugin1==1.0"],
233	    "urls": {
234	      "repository": "https://github.com/foo/bar"
235	    },
236	    "authors": [{
237	      "email": "user@example.com"
238	    }]
239	  }
240	}
241	```
242	
243	And the entry stub:
244	
245	
246	```py
247	from ida_plugin1.ida_plugin import PLUGIN_ENTRY
248	```
249	
250	### "Fat" Binary Plugin Archives
251	
252	Plugin archives can contain multiple compiled versions of a plugin, e.g., `foo-plugin.so` and `foo-plugin.dylib`.
253	In this case, the entry point must specify the bare path to the plugin, e.g., `foo-plugin`, and IDA will append the appropriate extension based on the platform.
254	You don't have to support all platforms. It's acceptable to publish multiple "thin" archives, one for each platform; however, "fat" archives are convenient.
255	
256	The file extensions must be exactly:
257	
258	  - `.dll` - Windows x86-64
259	  - `.so` - Linux 86-64
260	  - `_x86_64.dylib` - macOS x86_64 (not yet supported by IDA)
261	  - `_aarch64.dylib` - macOS aarch64 (not yet supported by IDA)
262	  - `.dylib` - macOS Universal Binary, only if Intel/ARM dylibs aren't present. (note: you must use this for macOS currently)
263	
264	
265	
266	Remember, plugin names must be unique within a plugin archive, which means:
267	
268	Allowed:
269	```
270	root/
271	  plugin/
272	    ida-plugin.json (name: foo-plugin)
273	    foo-plugin.so
274	    foo-plugin.dylib
275	    foo-plugin.dll
276	```
277	
278	Disallowed:
279	```
280	root/
281	  plugin-linux/
282	    ida-plugin.json (name: foo-plugin)
283	    foo-plugin.so
284	  plugin-windows/
285	    ida-plugin.json (name: foo-plugin)  <-- name collides!
286	    foo-plugin.dll
287	```
288	
289	### (uncommon) Multi-Plugin Archives
290	
291	Because the `ida-plugin.json` file marks the root of a plugin within the archive, an archive can contain multiple plugins:
292	
293	```
294	plugins.zip
295	├── plugin1
296	│   ├── plugin1.py
297	│   └── ida-plugin.json
298	└── plugin2
299	    ├── plugin2.py
300	    └── ida-plugin.json
301	```
302	
303	Plugin archives can also be collected into a [plugin bundle](./plugin-bundle-spec.md) for offline installation on air-gapped machines.
304	
305

1	# IDA Plugin Manager
2	
3	The IDA Plugin Manager handles searching, installing, upgrading, and removing IDA plugins. It works with both IDAPython and native (C/C++) plugins.
4	
5	Community plugins are indexed from public GitHub repositories and served through the Hex-Rays portal. Hex-Rays also publishes private plugins available to users with active IDA licenses. Browse available plugins at [plugins.hex-rays.com](https://plugins.hex-rays.com).
6	
7	!!! note "Development status"
8	
9	      The plugin manager is complete, and we’re now in the process of packaging plugins. Documentation updates are ongoing, and minor adjustments are expected.
